transcript.en: OK, Stewart.
transcript.zh: Stewart

transcript.en: We need to start planning our paper on public libraries.
transcript.zh: 我们得开始计划关于公共图书馆的论文了。

transcript.en: Have you thought of an angle yet?
transcript.zh: 你想到从哪个角度写了吗？

transcript.en: Well, there's so much we could look into.
transcript.zh: 嗯，有很多可以着手的东西。

transcript.en: How libraries have changed over the centuries,for instance,or
transcript.zh: 比如图书馆在过去的世纪里是如何变迁的，比如说，或者

transcript.en: how different countries organise them.
transcript.zh: 各个国家对它们的组织有何不同。

transcript.en: What do you think, Trudie?
transcript.zh: 你觉得怎么样，Trudie.

transcript.en: Maybe we should concentrate on this country, and try and relate the changes in libraries to external developments, like the fact that far more people can read than a century ago,
transcript.zh: 也许我们应该聚焦于这个国家，试着把图书馆的变化与外部发展情况联系起来， 比如相较于100年前现在有更多的人识字。

transcript.en: and that the local population may speak lots of different languages.
transcript.zh: 当地的人可能说着很多不同语言的事实。

transcript.en: We could include something about changes in the source of funding, too.
transcript.zh: 我们也可以纳入一些有关图书馆资金来源变化的东西。

transcript.en: Yes, but remember we're only supposed to write a short paper, so it's probably best if we don't go into funding in any detail.
transcript.zh: 是的，但要记住我们要写的是一篇短论文，所以在资金方面最好不要有任何详述。

transcript.en: Right. Well, shall we just brainstorm a few ideas, to get started?
transcript.zh: 嗯。我们现在开始对几个想法头脑风暴一下就开始好吗？

transcript.en: OK. We obviously need to look at the impact of new technology, particularly the internet.
transcript.zh: 好的，很明显我们需要考虑新技术，尤其是互联网的影响。

transcript.en: Now that lots of books have been digitalised, people can access them from their own computers at home.
transcript.zh: 因为很多书籍都已经数字化了，所以人们在家通过自己的电脑就能读到它们。

transcript.en: And if everyone did that, libraries would be obsolete.
transcript.zh: 如果所有人都那样，图书馆就要被淘汰了。

transcript.en: Yes.
transcript.zh: 是的

transcript.en: But the digitalised books that are available online for free are mostly out of copyright.aren't they?
transcript.zh: 但那些可以在网上找到的数字化的书大多都是版权过期了的，是不是？

transcript.en: And copyright in this country lasts for 70 years after the author dies.
transcript.zh: 在这个国家，版权在作者死后可持续70年。

transcript.en: So you won't find the latest best-seller or up-to-date information.
transcript.zh: 所以，你不会在网上找到最近的畅销书或者最新的信息。

transcript.en: That's an important point.
transcript.zh: 这一点很重要。

transcript.en: Anyway, I find it hard to concentrate when I'm reading a long text on a screen.
transcript.zh: 不管怎么样，我发现我在屏幕上看一段长文本时很难集中注意力。

transcript.en: I'd much rather read a physical book.
transcript.zh: 我宁愿看实体书，

transcript.en: And it takes longer to read on a screen.
transcript.zh: 而且在屏幕上看书要花更长时间。

transcript.en: Oh, I prefer it.
transcript.zh: 啊，我更喜欢在屏幕上看书，

transcript.en: I suppose it's Just a personal preference.
transcript.zh: 我想这只是个人偏好问题。

transcript.en: Mm. I expect that libraries will go on evolving in the next few years.
transcript.zh: 嗯，我预计在接下来的几年里图书馆将继续演变。

transcript.en: Some have already become centres where community activities take place, like local clubs meeting there.
transcript.zh: 有的图书馆已经变成开展社区活动的中心了，就像是本地社团聚会一样。

transcript.en: I think that' ll become even more common.
transcript.zh: 我认为这会变得更加普遍。

transcript.en: I'd like to think so, and that they'll still be serving their traditional function, but I'm not so sure.
transcript.zh: 我认同，同时它们仍然会发挥自己的传统功能，不过我不是很确定。

transcript.en: There are financial implications, after all.
transcript.zh: 毕竟还有财务方面的考量。

transcript.en: What I'm afraid will happen is that books and magazines will all disappear and there II just be rows and rows of computers.
transcript.zh: 我害怕发生的是书籍和杂志都会消失，只剩下一排排的电脑。

transcript.en: They won't look anything like the libraries we're used to.
transcript.zh: 那样的话它们就丝毫不像我们所习惯的图书馆了。

transcript.en: Well, we'll see.
transcript.zh: 好吧，我们会看到的.

transcript.en: I've just had an idea.
transcript.zh: 我刚刚有了个想法。

transcript.en: Why don't we make an in-depth study of our local public library as background to our paper?
transcript.zh: 我们为什么不对本地的公共图书馆做一个深入研究，作为我们论文的背景资料呢？

transcript.en: Yes, that'd be interesting, and raise all sorts of issues.
transcript.zh: 嗯，那会很有趣，而且能引申出所有的问题。

transcript.en: Let's make a list of possible things we could ask about, then work out some sort of structure.
transcript.zh: 我们就可能会问到的事情列一个表吧，然后琢磨出问题的结构来。

transcript.en: For instance. um. we could interview some of the staff,
transcript.zh: 比如说，我们可以采访一些图书馆职员，

transcript.en: and find out whether the library has its own budget, or if that's controlled by the local council.
transcript.zh: 问清楚图书馆是否有自己的预算，还是由当地市政厅控制。

transcript.en: And what their policies are.
transcript.zh: 还有他们那的规矩是怎样的。

transcript.en: I know they don't allow food,
transcript.zh: 我知道他们不允许在里面吃东西，

transcript.en: but I'd love to find out what types of noise they ban-there always seems to be a lot of talking, but never music.
transcript.zh: 但我还想知道的是他们会禁止什么样的噪音，那里似乎总是有很多人说话，但从来没有音乐。

transcript.en: I don't know if that's a policy or it just happens.
transcript.zh: 我不知道那是图书馆的规矩，还是只是碰巧。

transcript.en: Ah, I've often wondered.
transcript.zh: 嗯，我也经常好奇。

transcript.en: Then there are things like how the library is affected by employment laws.
transcript.zh: 然后就是图书馆是怎样受雇佣法律影响的。

transcript.en: I suppose there are rules about working hours. facilities for staff.and so on.
transcript.zh: 我想关于工作时间、图书馆员工设施等都有相关的规程。

transcript.en: Right.Then there are other issues relating to the design of the building and how customers use it.
transcript.zh: 是的。再有就是有关建筑设计和客人怎么使用它的问题。

transcript.en: Like what measures does the library take to ensure their safety?
transcript.zh: 比如说图书馆采取了什么措施来保证人们的安全。

transcript.en: They'd need floor coverings that aren't slippery, and emergency exits, for instance.
transcript.zh: 比如说他们得有不滑的地板和紧急出口。

transcript.en: Oh, and another thing-there's the question of the kind of insurance the library needs to have, in case anyone gets injured.
transcript.zh: 啊，还有个问题，图书馆需要买什么种类的保险，以防有人受伤。

transcript.en: Yes, that's something else to find out.
transcript.zh: 嗯，这个问题也得弄清楚。

transcript.en: You know something I've often wondered?
transcript.zh: 你知道我经常好奇什么吗？

transcript.en: What's that?
transcript.zh: 什么？

transcript.en: Well, you know they've got an archive of local newspapers going back years?
transcript.zh: 嗯，你知道他们有本地报纸很多年的存档吗？

transcript.en: Well, next to it they've got the diary of a well-known politician from the late 19th century.
transcript.zh: 此外，他们还有一位19世纪晚期著名政客的日记。

transcript.en: I wonder why it's there.
transcript.zh: 我想知道为什么它在那。

transcript.en: Do you know what his connection was with this area?
transcript.zh: 你知道他跟这片区域有什么联系吗？

transcript.en: No idea. Let's add it to our list of things to find out.
transcript.zh: 不知道。我们把它加到我们要弄清楚的事情列表里吧。

transcript.en: Oh, I've just thought - you know people might ask in the library about local organisations like sports clubs?
transcript.zh: 啊，我刚刚想到 - 你知道人们会在图书馆问一些有关本地组织的事情吗，比如说体育俱乐部。

transcript.en: Well. I wonder if they keep a database. or whether they just look online.
transcript.zh: 我想知道他们是不是有一个数据库，或者他们只是在网上查的。

transcript.en: Right. I quite fancy finding out what the differences are between a library that's open to the public and one that's part of a museum,for example-they must be very different.
transcript.zh: 嗯。我也很想知道向公众开放的图书馆，跟比如说属于博物馆一部分的图书馆有什么不同，它们一定非常不同。

transcript.en: Mmm. Then something else I'd like to know is…
transcript.zh: 嗯，我还想知道的事情是...
